summary: CS content is deep and renders cleanly at every device size, but its practice layers have systematic faults: multiple-choice answers sit at A/B 94% of the time, bank files duplicate past-paper questions already authored as worked cards, and ~30 decks ask one fact twice. The inventory pass found that the self-mark tally, not just the content, misjudges marks: examFromWorked turns the one-line Answer summary into a tickable mark and ignores each step's own weight, so 60 CS items cannot reach full marks from their real points, and IT schemes give one checkbox per two marks. IT is the weak side: the generated spec dumps garbled assessment-criteria text into the last leaf of each unit and duplicates F206.6.1, F201 has no worked answers and almost no examiner intel, the IT desk's 'Start here' points at the finished F200, and its boundary card collapses on iPad portrait. Shared presentation gaps: the worked card's 'Write it out' pill covers titles on iPhone, the reading place is lost on any detour (a notes diagram, then Back, reopens page 1), and syntax colours are nearly invisible in the light shop theme Washi Morning. Root causes: authoring without automated checks (no near-duplicate, answer-position, mark-sum or validate_content gate), mark weights kept as display text, the IT parser's missing section boundaries, and view-local or dark-tuned state that was never generalised.

findings.title: IT spec text for F206.6.1, F204.6.5, F202.5.1, F201.5.2, F200.5.3 (and F200.2.x/F202.2.x) holds garbled PDF dumps of the assessment criteria
findings.detail: The generated IT spec (js/data/it.js) contains multi-thousand-character strings of shuffled PDF text in the Spec tab content/info lists for the last leaf of each unit: e.g. F206.6.1 'Ways to reflect' ends with a 2,271-char 'Lessons learnt Assessment criteria The table below gives...' string and a 2,884-char info item; F204.6.5 has 2,164/1,007/2,510-char strings; F202.5.1 2,330/538/2,502; F201.5.2 (the unit the user is sitting) has 'Urban and community planning Assessment guidance This unit is assessed by an exam...' and an 831-char run; F200.5.3 876 chars. Shorter merged rows also start with a dangling 'include:' (F200.2.2, F200.2.3, F200.2.6, F201.2.4, F202.2.2, F202.2.4, F202.2.5, F202.3.3). Column-interleaved words ('The tasks. means that the unit grade awarded') are unreadable on the Spec tab and pollute search and the Assistant's spec reads. F206 is the NEA the user is doing now. Beyond the long dumps, 189 short spec rows in 39 IT leaves are fragments ('□ Does', '□ Techniques To', '• Diagnostic Prescriptive □', a bare '□'), e.g. F201.2.3 Data mining techniques reads ['□ Data mining','□ Data mining techniques','• Descriptive','• Diagnostic Prescriptive □','□','□ Does','□'] and F201.2.6 omits 'Factor analysis' which the notes teach.
findings.fix: Fix tools/gen_data.py's IT parser to stop each leaf at the 'Assessment criteria'/'Assessment guidance'/'Synoptic assessment' headings and at page-column breaks, and to join 'To include:' continuation lines into bullet rows; regenerate it.js (invariant 24) and add a smoke check that no IT spec string exceeds ~300 chars or starts with 'include:'.
findings.rootCause: PDF parser in tools/gen_data.py appends trailing unit-level sections (criteria tables, guidance, synoptic tables) to the last topic leaf and mis-splits two-column 'To include' boxes.
findings.recheck: holds: js/data/it.js:2246-2283 unchanged on f84962c; content-cs-it/dump.json re-generated and metrics byte-identical; search for 'Lessons learnt Assessment criteria' still matches F206.6.1 (the dump is indexed).

findings.title: Quiz answers are guessable: the correct option is A or B in 94% of CS questions (D only 12 of 1,347) and options are never shuffled
findings.detail: Across all 1,347 CS quiz questions the correct index is A 677, B 590, C 68, D 12; IT's 288 are A 17, B 211, C 57, D 3. The correct option is also the uniquely longest one in 688/1,347 CS (51%) and 201/288 IT (70%) questions, against ~25% by chance. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders item.opts in authored order (only the question order has a Shuffle), so a learner quickly learns 'pick A/B, pick the longest', and 'Quiz best' on the topic inspector and RAG overstate recall. 46 leaves have 60%+ of answers in one position (e.g. 4.4.1.3: 11 of 12 are A; 4.5.2.1 9/11 A).
findings.evidence: node content-cs-it/quiz.js over dump.json: compsci [677,590,68,12], it [17,211,57,3]; longest-correct compsci 688/1347, it 201/288; js/engines/quiz.js:88 item.opts.forEach renders in authored order (shuffle at :25 is only applied to question order, :66)
findings.fix: Shuffle each question's options at render with a deterministic per-question seed (map ans through the permutation; keep keyboard 1–4 on the displayed order) and rebalance the longest-option bias by trimming correct options or lengthening distractors in the authored banks; add a smoke check that no leaf has >50% of answers at one index after shuffling is off.
findings.rootCause: Authoring habit (answer written first) plus an engine that never permutes options.
findings.recheck: holds: content-cs-it/quiz.js re-run → compsci [677,590,68,12], it [17,211,57,3]; the Quiz tab's Shuffle (js/engines/quiz.js:66) reorders questions only, options still render in authored order (:88).

findings.detail: Every Haskell listing in 4.12.x (map/filter/fold definitions, partial application, composition, list processing — 11 blocks) is a {code} with lang 'text', so its head says 'text' and nothing is highlighted, while the C# twin beside it is coloured; the 4.7.3.5 assembly blocks print 'asm' because LANG_NAME has no entry for it.

findings.fix: Tag those blocks lang 'haskell' and add 'haskell: "Haskell"', 'asm: "AQA assembly"' to LANG_NAME with a small keyword set in highlightCode (comments --, ::, ->).

findings.title: Derived exam items make the worked card's one-line 'Answer:' summary a tickable mark point, so full marks can be self-awarded with a real point missing
findings.detail: KOS.content.examFromWorked pushes '**Answer:** <result>' as the last ms bullet of every exam item it derives from a worked card (801 of the 1,194 CS exam items). The exam engine treats every ms bullet as a tickable mark point: when points > marks (729 items) the award is min(total, ticks), so ticking the Answer summary replaces a real mark point; when points == marks (29 items) the Answer line IS one of the marks. Repro: 4.6.2.1 Exam questions, Q6 'AQA June 2017 · P2 Q04.2' (3 marks): leave 'There may not be a compiler…' unticked, tick the other three points and 'Answer: No translator; constrained hardware' → AWARDED 3 / 3. Example of the == case: 4.7.3.5 'June 2017 · P2 Q07.1' (4 marks) has three 1-mark steps + Answer = 4 'points', so the summary is the fourth mark.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/exam-4621-q042-selfmark-mac.png; kos eval (exam2.js): allStepsNoAnswer 3, oneStepMissingButAnswer 3; js/core/content.js:568 (ms.push('**Answer:** '…)); js/engines/quiz.js:288 perMark, :294 fromTicks min(total,n); node count over dump.json: derivedWithAnswer 801, pointsGtMarks 729, pointsEqMarks 29
findings.fix: Render the Answer line as a non-tickable 'Model answer' row (e.g. ms item {answer:true} or a separate `answer` field on the item) and exclude it from points.length; re-check 4.7.3.5 Q07.1 which then has 3 points for 4 marks (see the mark-sum finding).
findings.rootCause: examFromWorked mixes the model answer into the mark-scheme array that the tally counts.

findings.title: Restoring an older backup folds a merged CS leaf's progress by dropping it: a completed member leaf loses to a weaker record on the kept leaf
findings.detail: The twelve CS merges fold old leaves into one kept leaf (store.js REF_ALIASES, e.g. 4.5.1.2–4.5.1.7 → 4.5.1.1). renameRefs() renames a stored key only when the kept key is absent; otherwise it DELETES the member's record. Fixture via KOS.store.replaceState (the same scrubLegacy gate as import and every cloud pull): progress {4.5.1.1: conf 1, covered}, {4.5.1.3: conf 3, status done, all four checks}, {4.5.1.5: conf 3, studied} → after the gate only {4.5.1.1: conf 1, covered} remains — the completed 4.5.1.3 and the studied 4.5.1.5 are gone, and the topic reads Red/barely started. Any backup or cloud document from before the merges (2 Oct 2026), or from a device that had not yet booted the new build, loses the member leaves' progress, notes and confidence on restore.
findings.evidence: node audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/content-cs-it/alias2.js → replaceState-> {"compsci:4.5.1.1":{"conf":1,"checks":{"covered":true}}}, lastRef 4.4.1.5→4.4.1.3; js/core/store.js:371-374 (if (!hasOwnProperty(o, nk)) o[nk] = o[k]; delete o[k]); store.js:318-323 comment 'the kept leaf's wins'
findings.fix: For the progress/notes/quiz maps, merge the member record into the kept one (max checks, max conf, best status, concatenated notes) instead of discarding it; keep 'kept wins' only for scalar fields that conflict. Add a smoke case with three members and a weak kept record.
findings.rootCause: A generic key rename with 'kept wins' semantics is applied to records that should be combined.

findings.title: On iPhone a worked example keeps its 84px 'GIVEN / STEP n' label column, squeezing the working into 61% of the card
findings.detail: Every worked-example row is a three-column grid (label · body · mark chip) with a fixed 84px label column at every width. At iPhone (402) the card is 370px wide: label 84px + 12px gap, the body starts at x130 and is 226px wide, and a mark chip takes the right edge, so algebra, truth-table rows and mark-scheme notes wrap every 3–4 words while the column under 'STEP 1' stays empty for the whole step. CS notes hold 941 worked cards, so this is most of the reading on the phone. The label is a one-word kicker that could sit above the body.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/recheck-writeout-4641-iphone.png (4.6.4.1, 'Trace Figure 5 and write G'); kos eval at iphone: card 370, label [34, 84], body [130, 226], gap 12; css/tokens.css:562 --wk-label-w: 84px; css/views/study.css:351 .k-n-wrow grid-template-columns: var(--wk-label-w) minmax(0,1fr) auto (no narrower tier)
findings.fix: Below 560px stack the row: the label as a small kicker on its own line (with the mark chip beside it), the body full width (a 560 tier in study.css, widest-first per invariant 48).
findings.rootCause: The worked-row grid has no phone tier.

findings.title: Self-mark tally ignores a worked step's own mark weight ('[3 marks]'), so 60 derived CS exam items cannot reach full marks from their real mark points
findings.detail: examFromWorked turns each worked step into one tickable mark point and only appends its weight as text (' [3 marks]'). The tally counts ticks equally: when points != marks it scales round(total*n/points). Examples: 4.7.3.5 'AS June 2019 · P2 Q10.1' (7 marks) has steps worth 3/1/1 plus the Answer line = 4 points: ticking every real step gives round(7*3/4)=5 of 7, and only ticking the Answer summary reaches 7; ticking just the 3-mark step gives 2. 'AS June 2017 · P2 Q07.1' (4 marks) has three 1-mark steps, so full marks require ticking the Answer summary. Over the dump, 60 derived CS items have fewer real mark points than marks and 34 carry a step weighted >1. The −/+ stepper lets the user override, but the default award is wrong.
findings.evidence: js/core/content.js:547-552 (ms line + ' [' + st.mk + ']'), js/engines/quiz.js:288-295 (perMark, fromTicks scaling); js/data/content/cs-p2-47b.js:355-375; node over content-cs-it/dump.json: derived items 801, realPoints<marks 60, weighted steps 34 (4.5.3.1, 4.5.4.5, 4.5.4.7, 4.5.5.3, 4.5.6.1 …)
findings.fix: Carry the step weight as data (ms item {t, w}) and let fromTicks sum weights; author the missing final mark point where a worked card's steps add up to fewer marks than its src (e.g. 4.7.3.5 Q07.1 needs a 'whole loop correct' point); add a smoke check that step weights sum to the src marks.
findings.rootCause: Mark weights are stored as free text in st.mk and flattened into display text; the tally has no notion of a point's weight.

findings.title: Back from a notes diagram (or any detour) reopens the topic's notes on page 1, losing the reading place
findings.detail: The 34 'Interactive diagram · Open simulation →' buttons in CS notes navigate to #/sims/<id>. Coming back (browser Back, or the lab's 'Open topic page') reopens the Notes tab on page 1, not the page the diagram sat on. Repro: 4.2.1.1 Notes, page 3 of 7 holds the Linked list diagram; click it (hash #/sims/tl-list), history.back() → #/ref/compsci/4.2.1.1, Notes tab, page select '0'. Long CS leaves have 6–10 pages, so every detour (diagram, a sim, a search hit, a bell click) sends the reader back to the start.
findings.evidence: kos eval content-cs-it/diagback.js at mac: {pg:2, h1:'#/sims/tl-list', back:'#/ref/compsci/4.2.1.1', tab:'Notes7', page:'0'}; js/modules/hub.js:2983 (cur = o.keep ? notePage : 0 — notePage is a closure variable that does not survive re-entering the view); js/core/content.js:450-453 (diagram click → KOS.sims.open)
findings.fix: Remember the note page per topic per device (state.ui.notePage['sid:ref'], like state.ui.lastProd) and reopen on it; or open the diagram's lab in a dialog/side pane over the notes (KOS.sims.embed already exists).
findings.rootCause: The reader page is view-local state, reset on every KOS.show of the topic.

findings.detail: Every CS code listing (152 code blocks: C#, SQL, pseudocode, assembly) colours its tokens with --syn-kw/--syn-num/--syn-str. tokens.css tunes them for a dark ground and only Atelier Dawn restates them for a light one; Washi Morning, the one light shop theme (--bg l 0.948), inherits the dark-ground values. findings.title: IT desk on iPad portrait: the qualification boundary bar collapses to 48px, its 120/180/240/270 labels print on top of each other

findings.title: IT desk's 'Start here' sends you to F200.1.1, a unit already sat and with no notes, instead of F201/F206

findings.title: Six CS quizzes ask the identical question twice (same stem, same answer), e.g. 4.9.4.6 '172.32.0.5 is' as Q1 and Q2
findings.detail: Exact duplicate quiz items in one leaf: 4.9.4.5 Q1/Q2 'IPv6 addresses are written in', 4.9.4.6 Q1/Q2 '172.32.0.5 is' (byte-identical object), 4.9.4.7 Q1/Q2 'Why avoid DHCP for a server reached by port forwarding?', 4.9.4.8 Q1/Q2 'NAT is performed by', 4.9.4.9 Q1/Q2 'Port forwarding is configured on', 4.13.1.4 Q1/Q5 'For a valid range 1–10, which is boundary data?' (options reordered). The learner answers the same question back to back and the score counts it twice; the 4.9.4.x quizzes are already only 5 questions, so 20% of each is a repeat. Not covered by the flashcard redundancy finding (that measured flashcards and exam items only).
findings.evidence: node over dump.json (exact lower-cased stem match): 7 pairs in 7 leaves, 6 with the same answer; js/data/content/cs-p2-49c.js:358-359 (two identical lines)
findings.fix: Replace the second item in each pair with a new question on another point of the leaf (4.9.4.6: a 10.x or 192.168.x address; 4.9.4.9: what a forwarded port maps to). Add an exact-duplicate check to the content lint.
findings.rootCause: Copy-paste during authoring; no duplicate check in smoke65/66.

findings.title: A third of quiz explanations say nothing: 502 of 1,635 'why' lines are under 16 characters ('Definition.' ×44, 'See the notes.' ×10, 'Spec.' ×6)
findings.detail: The quiz shows `why` after every answer ('✕ Not quite · <why>'), the moment a learner who got it wrong needs the reason. 502 of 1,635 CS+IT explanations are under 16 characters: 'Definition.' (44), 'See the notes.' (10), 'Spec.' (6), 'NE per mark scheme.' (4), 'Spec wording.', 'Notation.', 'Absorption.'. Worst leaves: 4.6.4.1 (11), 4.9.4.6 (9), 4.5.4.5, 4.9.4.9 and 4.12.2.1 (8 each), 4.4.2.2, 4.7.1.1, 4.7.3.3, 4.9.1.2, 4.9.2.3, 4.9.4.1, 4.9.4.5, 4.9.4.7, 4.13.1.3, 4.13.1.4 (7 each). 'NE per mark scheme' is mark-scheme shorthand (not enough) that the learner is not told about.
findings.evidence: node over dump.json: total 1635, why.length<16: 502; js/engines/quiz.js:123-125 (why rendered after '✕ Not quite · '); js/data/content/cs-p2-49c.js:358
findings.fix: Rewrite short explanations as one sentence that says why the right option is right AND why the tempting wrong one is wrong; lint why.length >= 25 in the content gate.

findings.title: IT exam mark schemes give one bullet per two marks, so the tally awards IT answers in steps of 2 (97 of 150 items)
findings.detail: IT exam items write '(1) … (1)' inside one bullet (e.g. F201.2.2 'Describe two ways this could be handled [4]': two bullets 'Deletion (1): remove the rows … (1).'). The tally has one checkbox per bullet and scales, so ticking one bullet awards 2 and there is no way to tick the one mark earned for naming a method without describing it. 97 of the 150 IT exam items have fewer bullets than marks; the 9-mark NEA-practice items use '(1–2)' bullets the same way. The question text also repeats the tariff ('… handled. [4]') next to the '4 marks' header chip.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/content-cs-it/it-f2022-exam-selfmark-mac.png (one tick → AWARDED 2 / 4); kos eval content-cs-it/itex.js: points 2, afterOneTick '2'; js/data/content/it-f201.js exam arrays; js/engines/quiz.js:294
findings.fix: Split IT mark-scheme bullets into one point per mark (the '(1)' markers give the split), and strip trailing '[n]' from IT question text.
findings.rootCause: IT content authored mark schemes as prose bullets per idea rather than per mark.
